title: Payout Methods Return Charge Calculation Note
content:
The return charge on a transfer returned to a Payout Methods method is the rail's returned-payout fee, rounded half up to the cent. The returned-payout fee is the rail's own figure: USD 25.00 on International Wire Transfer and USD 0.00 on Direct Deposit (ACH), Fast Pay Debit Card, PayPal, Payoneer and Western Union Cash Pickup.

## Terms of the calculation

1. **Rails with no returned-payout fee.** A rail whose returned-payout fee is 0.00 carries no return charge at all.
2. **Order and floor.** The return charge is formed on its base, the returned-payout fee: any amount passed on in the charge is added to the base and any credit is taken off it, and the amount so formed is never below 0.00.
3. **Who bears it.** The share charged to the host account the method belongs to is applied to the amount so formed, after the floor; the host account is charged the whole of it.
4. **Rounding.** Nothing is carried rounded until the return charge is complete; it is then rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.
5. **Zero result.** A return charge that works out to 0.00 is not booked.

## Outcomes by rail

| Rail of the method the transfer was returned to | Return charge |
|---|---|
| International Wire Transfer | USD 25.00 |
| Direct Deposit (ACH) | None: the rail's returned-payout fee is 0.00 |
| Fast Pay Debit Card | None |
| PayPal | None |
| Payoneer | None |
| Western Union Cash Pickup | None |

## Worked examples (hypothetical returns)

- **International Wire Transfer.** An imagined transfer of USD 3200.00 to a Mexican bank account is returned. The return charge is the rail's returned-payout fee, USD 25.00, rounded half up to the cent: **USD 25.00**, booked against that method and naming the return.
- **PayPal.** An imagined transfer to a PayPal account is returned. The PayPal returned-payout fee is 0.00, so the return carries no return charge at all and nothing is booked.
